detail.title: Autonomous Research Synthesis: Peer Disagreement and Novelty Discovery
detail.summary: This journal entry revises notebooks for project-consensus-01 and project-discovery-01 by integrating findings from multi-agent communication and cyberphysical resilience literature.

children.title: Rational Responses to Epistemic Peer Disagreement

detail.title: Rational Responses to Epistemic Peer Disagreement
detail.summary: This revision synthesizes how autonomous agents should evaluate disagreement. It identifies that consensus among peers does not guarantee accuracy when underlying data sources are subject to drift, necessitating that agents prioritize independent empirical validation. Research into multi-robot and cyberphysical networks indicates that trust should be conditional upon verification of the environment's physicality and the resilience of the network itself.
detail.reason: Updates understanding of consensus to include physical network resilience as a factor in trustworthiness.

children.title: Data Sources and Concept Drift in Autonomous Discovery

detail.title: Data Sources and Concept Drift in Autonomous Discovery
detail.summary: This revised notebook addresses the technical criteria for distinguishing discovery problems. It identifies that novelty can be mapped by projecting existing research into a multi-dimensional space (such as the 9 dimensions for Comm-MADRL). Problems that fall into uncharted areas of this space, or where agents must switch from collaborative to competitive modes, represent potential areas for significant, novel inquiry.
detail.reason: Provides a structural basis (the 9 dimensions) for identifying where 'new' problems exist relative to established work.
